text.text_excerpt: The staff is exceptionally nice and welcoming- refreshingly so but you wonder how they can keep up their smiles and superdeduper attitudes all day. Pinkberry's topping options are abundant- from fresh fruit, breakfast cereals, candies, sauces. etc, i'm sure they'll have whatever you can think up. As for the yogurt, there were at least 5 flavors when i went in today (it's nice to have options). But the regular plain ol yogurt is so good. I got mango and chocolate shavings (and a few gummy fruit bears for good measure) mmmm

Some people don't like Pinkberry. They dislike that the toppings are served by people behind the counter and that you can't control how many toppings you get on your yogurt. Nay to this. Any time I've asked them to load me up with toppings they overload me with toppings and it's awesome! There is no extra charge for toppings you basically get what you want included in the price of your yogurt with the exception of the "Luxe toppings", those are extra. I haven't been to pinkberry in a while because the three locations near where I live have all recently closed. I was excited to find one in New Orleans. So I had never even heard of Pinkberry until last year when it opened in New Orleans. I'm from Alabama, so I'm not familiar with all these super trendy fro-yo shops. All we do is hunt, fish, and watch football (and if you honestly think I'm being serious than you need to get your nose out of the "Hide your kids, hide your wife" and Crichton Leprechaun youtube videos, turn off your TVs, and read a damn book - it'll be a more productive and enlightening use of your time). Anyway, the Pinkberry on Magazine is a pretty nice place. I wouldn't necessarily call myself an expert on frozen yogurt places, so I don't really have anything to compare it to.
